questions_and_answers.question: Which mood is used in the clause 'Der Arzt glaubt, dass ich krank bin'?
The article suggests that the forms of the subjunctive in indirect discourse are used to:

answers.answer: Underline the fact they are the speaker's own views
Underline they are the views of another

articles.text:
B. INDIRECT DISCOURSE

I. The forms of the subjunctive based on the Past Tense are often used in Indirect Discourse situations.
Er sagte, ich bekäme den Führerschein.
Ich hörte, es ließe sich leicht machen.

In Indirect Discourse one can state the content of another's words, thoughts or wishes with the subjunctive and thus underline the fact that those are the views of another. It may be evident from the statement that one wishes to divorce himself from the views: Er glaubt, der Mond bestünde aus grünem Käse. Or one may simply be reporting a fact: Er sagt, der Konsul käme morgen zurück.

If one wishes to endorse the views or words of another, one uses the indicative: Der Arzt glaubt, dass ich krank bin.
One may mark the subjective nature of his own views by the use of the subjunctive or simply use the subjunctive in stating his own views because one wishes to state them indirectly.
Ich dachte, er ginge.
Ich habe immer gedacht, dass er es wüsste.
